title: Driving GitHub Actions from the Terminal
intro: You can monitor, trigger, and debug pipelines entirely from the terminal — faster than clicking through the web UI, and scriptable.

steps.prompt: List the workflows defined in this repository.
steps.fake_output:
NAME          STATE   ID
CI            active  48213
Deploy        active  48214
Nightly Scan  active  48215
steps.why: The names here are what you pass to 'gh workflow run' and 'gh run list --workflow'.

steps.prompt: Manually trigger the Deploy workflow for the staging environment.
steps.fake_output: ✓ Created workflow_dispatch event for deploy.yml at main
steps.explanation: -f passes an input defined under 'on: workflow_dispatch: inputs:'.
steps.why: Only works if the workflow declares a workflow_dispatch trigger. Manual triggers with inputs are the standard pattern for 'deploy this to that environment' buttons.

steps.prompt: Watch the run you just started, live, until it finishes.
steps.fake_output:
✓ build   in 1m12s
✓ test    in 2m03s
* deploy  (running)
...
✓ Run Deploy (9876543) completed with 'success'
steps.explanation: Streams job status updates in your terminal.
steps.why: Add --exit-status to make the command's exit code reflect the run result — handy for chaining: 'gh run watch --exit-status && ./smoke-test.sh'.

steps.prompt: A CI run (ID 9876500) failed. View only the logs from the failed steps.
steps.fake_output:
test  Run npm test  FAIL src/cart.test.js
  ● applies discount › rounds to 2 decimals
    Expected: 19.99
    Received: 19.990000000000002
steps.explanation: Straight to the failing assertion — a floating-point rounding bug.
steps.why: --log-failed skips thousands of lines of passing-step output. It's usually the first command to run after any red build.

steps.prompt: The failure was a known flaky network test. Re-run only the jobs that failed.
steps.explanation: Only failed jobs run again, reusing successful jobs' results.
steps.why: Faster and cheaper than re-running everything. But re-running flaky tests until they pass hides real problems — if a test needs rerunning regularly, fix or quarantine it (see cicd-incident-003).
